claim: `include_website_name` lacks the `?` suffix so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it, and website_name is not in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is always serialized, exposing TL0 users' websites to anonymous visitors that `website` deliberately hides.
body: ## [ISSUE] `website_name` bypasses the TL0/anonymous restriction that hides `website` **Severity:** HIGH — anti-spam protection for TL0 profile websites is bypassed; the site name is rendered to anonymous viewers. ### The Problem ```ruby def include_website_name website.present? end ``` ActiveModel::Serializers only looks up `include_?` (with the question mark) — see the conventions used elsewhere in this same file (`include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge?`, and the `define_method "include_#{attr}?"` in `staff_attributes`/`private_attributes`/`untrusted_attributes`, lines 9, 18, 27). `include_website_name` is never invoked, so `website_name` is emitted for every user. More importantly, `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (line ~94), whose generated `include_website?` returns `false` when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` — i.e. the user is TL0 and the viewer is anonymous (`lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60`). `website_name` is added to the plain `attributes` list, so it gets no such guard. ### What happens today vs. what breaks Before this PR the client derived `websiteName` from `model.website`, which was absent for TL0 users viewed anonymously, so nothing rendered. After this PR `user.hbs` gates on `model.website_name`, which is present. For a TL0 user `linkWebsite` is false (`model.isBasic`), so the template renders `{{model.website_name}}` — the spammer's domain (and, on same-domain sites, full path) is shown to logged-out visitors and crawlers. This is exactly what `untrusted_attributes` exists to prevent. ### Recommendation Put `website_name` under the same guard and drop the dead method: ```ruby untrusted_attributes :bio_raw, :bio_cooked, :bio_excerpt, :location, :website, :website_name, :profile_background, :card_background ``` (`untrusted_attributes` also enforces `send(attr).present?`, which covers the intent of `include_website_name`.) Add a spec asserting `json[:website_name]` is nil for a TL0 user with an anonymous guardian.

claim: The 'same parent domain' heuristic strips only the first label, so on shared/public-suffix hosts (e.g. forum at `myforum.herokuapp.com`, website `spam.herokuapp.com`, or `a.co.uk` vs `b.co.uk`) unrelated sites are treated as same-domain and their full path is displayed.
body:
## [ISSUE] Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated sites on shared suffixes as the same domain

**Severity:** LOW — cosmetic/trust display issue; unrelated websites get the "same site" full-path treatment.

### The Problem

```ruby
elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2
  website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(website.to_s).path : website_host
```

Any two hosts with the same label count (>2) and identical labels after the first are considered the same organization. That is wrong for public suffixes: `myforum.herokuapp.com` vs `spam.herokuapp.com`, `forum.github.io` vs `evil.github.io`, `forum.example.co.uk` isn't affected but `a.co.uk` vs `b.co.uk` is. In these cases the display shows `spam.herokuapp.com/some/path`, which is the same presentation used for genuinely internal links.

The heuristic is also asymmetric: website `www.example.com` with forum `example.com` falls to the `else` branch and shows only the host, while `example.com` with forum `forum.example.com` shows the full path.

### Research

The canonical way to determine "same registrable domain" is the Public Suffix List (https://publicsuffix.org/), available in Ruby via the `public_suffix` gem (`PublicSuffix.domain(host)`).

### Recommendation

Compare registrable domains instead of label counts:

```ruby
def website_name
  uri = URI(website.to_s) rescue nil
  return if uri.nil? || uri.host.nil?
  same = PublicSuffix.domain(uri.host) == PublicSuffix.domain(Discourse.current_hostname) rescue false
  same ? uri.host + uri.path : uri.host
end
```

or, if adding a dependency is undesirable, restrict the full-path display to an exact host match or `discourse_host.end_with?(".#{website_host}")`.
